newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast power seen steady despite fires.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast power seen steady despite fires.

text.p: Spot power prices along the U.S. West Coast held relatively steady Tuesday despite news that Southern California Edison had shut two 5,000 kilovolt transmission lines due to a fire near Los Angeles, industry sources said.
Any price impact from the shutdown lines was discounted when traders learned the lines were expected to be restored by Tuesday afternoon, power brokers and marketers said.
"It looks like it's going to be a very short-term thing," one source said.
Also, hot weather in the U.S. Southwest boosted short-term prices at the Palo Verde switchyard in Arizona, sources said.

At the California-Oregon Border (COB), prices for firm, peak next-day delivery were quoted little changed at $19.00-20.00. Traders said the COB prices were steadied by reports that the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) had not changed its next-day power offer from yesterday.
BPA was reported to be offering power at an average of about $19.19 per megawatt hour (MWh).
September COB power for firm, peak delivery was assessed steady to lower at $17.80-18.20 from discussion in a range of $18.00-18.50 on Monday, the sources said.
At the Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) delivery point in Washington, firm, peak electricity prices for next-day delivery were quoted at $17.00-18.00 from quotes at $16.00-18.00 on Monday.
September Mid-C electricity was pegged at $17.00-17.25 from a range of $17.00-17.50 on Monday, the sources said.
At Palo Verde (PV), next-day electricity for peak, firm delivery was valued higher at $24.50-27.00 from a range of $23.00-24.00 for Tuesday delivery, brokers and marketers said.
September PV was reported to have eased to $21.00-21.25 after a morning price rally from $21.00-21.50 Monday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
